Tuesday. Swati took me to the wellness circle again, and this time I made myself ask. Where does the monthly contribution go? Who runs it? Why can't members see accounts? The leader smiled and said, "Trust is part of the journey." That is not an answer. Tonight I searched the group's name with the word "complaints" and found two news reports and a post by an ex-member who was told to cut off her sister. I showed Swati. Swati said they were just bitter people. Maybe. But a group that goes cold when you ask where the money goes doesn't feel healthy to me. I'm not going on Thursday. Not deciding forever, only this week.

Dilnaz

In the market town of Karad, Vijay had been invited by his cousin Alka to a "rural uplift" group. They met in a rented room above the cloth shop and spoke movingly about helping farmers.
At the third meeting, Vijay raised his hand. "Where does the money from the membership go? Who's the head of the organisation? Can I meet someone who was in it before?"
The room went quiet. The speaker said, "Questions like that show a lack of faith." A few people shook their heads at Vijay.
That night he sat in the cyber cafe near the bus stand and searched the group's name. He found a local news report about a complaint filed against its founders and a thread where former members said they'd been shouted at for asking about accounts.
He showed Alka the next day. She read it twice. "They never told us any of this."
"They didn't want us asking," Vijay said.

qa.q: Where did Vijay search for the group's name?
qa.a: At the cyber cafe near the bus stand.

qa.q: How did Vijay feel when the room went quiet after his questions?
qa.a: He likely felt uncomfortable and suspicious, especially when people shook their heads at him.

qa.q: What else could Vijay and Alka do with what they found?
qa.a: They could share the news report with others in the group and talk to a trusted elder or local official before anyone pays more.

qa.q: How might Alka feel after reading the news report?
qa.a: Alka seems shaken and perhaps betrayed, saying they were never told any of it.

grounding: Shows the person asking about funds, leadership and former members and checking news and reviews, with the group's hostility to questions as a warning sign.
